chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no wudu (ablution) due because of madhy from desire, nor from erection, nor from kissing, nor from touching the private part, nor from lying together; and neither the garment nor the body is washed because of it.

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةِ: sexual desire as a cause associated with the discharge
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: pre-seminal fluid referred to in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does madhy require wudu (ablution) or washing the clothes and body in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that madhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution) and does not require washing the garment or the body. It addresses practical rulings of taharah and distinguishes madhy from substances that do obligate purification.
